title: Batteries
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
arc: The Last Week of the Century
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: The hardware store has sold out of batteries. A sign in the window says so. The strip draws the sign and the empty pegs. Wood buys a flashlight with no batteries and finds that right too.

panels.composition: Main street, the hardware store, a hand-lettered sign in the window drawn as blocks, a line of people. WOOD and BARNABY passing.

image.prompt: a small-town hardware store with a hand-lettered sign in its window and a short line of people outside, a young man and a dog passing in rain, black and white, no words

panels.composition: Inside: the battery pegs, empty, a hundred hooks with nothing on them.

image.prompt: close on a hardware store's peg wall with every battery hook empty, black and white, no words

panels.composition: Wood at the register with a flashlight. The CLERK.

image.prompt: a young man at a hardware store register holding a flashlight while the clerk looks at him, black and white, no words

panels.composition: Wood on the sidewalk with a flashlight that doesn't work. The dog. The street. He likes it that way.

image.prompt: a young man on a rainy sidewalk holding a flashlight and a leash, a small dog looking up at him, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: Y2K week. A flashlight with no batteries, on purpose.
